I ended up changing my rankings after the matching fair and I'm very grateful to be matched at my #1 placement choice. Throughout the matching fair, I found that a good chunk of the organizers that interviewed were less "prepared" than I was so to speak: they either had technical difficulties, were in noisy environments, or were completely unaware of the limited time they were given and they weren't given enough time to get to know me well. Only two out of the six organizers I met with seemed to approach the interview well, and one of them just so happened to the organization I was matched with. 

I believe this problem could easily be solved if organizers were also required to take InPlace & CareerEco training workshops so that they could better navigate the software and make better first impressions with prospective interns.

column17:
The way information was being distributed was a bit confusing, especially when it came to the submission of onboarding documents. 

For example, we were told the last day to submit our I-9 Part 1 was on May 22nd, but I got an email on May 29th that it was the last day to upload I-9 Part 2 documents to the Dropbox. I didn't receive notice that anything needed to be submitted until that day and I needed to wait on a reply to my email to get access to the Dropbox link, and the link to sign up for the I-9 Part 2 Zoom meeting. I was in the midst of a late night shift at my job when I received a reply. If I didn't already have a copy of my I-9 document saved to my phone, I would have been dropped from the program. 

I understand drip-feeding us information to avoid confusion, but it would have been helpful to have a place where all the links could be found ahead of time, especially for things with deadlines that if missed, could drop us from the program.

I think the matching process was mostly straightforward, the only part that was unclear was the interviews. 

When the interview slots were first made available, only a few of the organizations that I wanted to interview with had slots available, and we could only do 3 interviews. I emailed the hub about this but they didn't really have an answer for why/whether the sites I was looking to interview with would be present at the Matching Fair at all. In the end, I did get to interview with site that I was most interested in, but I was only able to grab a slot because I was religiously checking CareerEco to see if their interviews would open. 

I recently had the chance to speak with some of my fellow Career Launch interns and they agreed that the interview portion of the matching process was a bit confusing as well.

Additionally, I live in Upper Manhattan and my job is 1hr and 15 minutes away from me. The only reason I didnt put in a request to change it is because I was warned that I could lose my acceptance and end up with nothing. I didn't apply to any other summer opportunities after getting this Healthcare acceptance in the Spring because I was under the impression that I would have a job and not to worry from previous meetings because everyone gets matched.So, I ultimately decided to take what I have, even though its far and move on because I need the money at the end of the day, and the institution I'm working at is really good so I am grateful. The very beginning of the Career Launch program I was excited. But everything onwards was just a mess. I was:
1. Unable to get messages from the Program: I had to rely on my friend who is also a part of the program to give me the dates and times of the meetings. I remember before the orientation of the prgram, I got an email of the link to the meeting 20 minutes before the actual program.

2. Unable to get an internship related to my major: I am an Electrical Engineer. I applied to 11 different opportunities and I got none of them. When I got assigned a place, it wasnt even related to my major at all. I even asked some of the students during the I-9 Part 2 meeting about my opportunity and they cant seem to understand how its related to STEM in any way.

3. Constantly facing many different bugs: A notable example would be when I was doing the I-9 section 1 form. I was unable to access it for a very long time because it kept displaying a message stating that the administrator has locked this page. I was able to eventually do it but I never got a confirmation that I did the form. This resulted me in almost being kicked from the program(I was later accepted back in to the program because I had a screenshot of the submission).

All in all, I am dissapointed with my time in this program. There were little to no good things that I could say.

column17: Communication from the marketing hub was often inconsistent and unclear. The need to submit hub assist forms to ask them questions rather than being able to email them directly slowed down the communications process during periods of time where the turnaround on deadlines were short. Additionally, I would occassionally receive contradictory answers from separate members of the hub staff, particularly in regards to how long I should wait before reaching out to my supervisor. Overall, I think the process would have greatly benefitted from additional transparency. I recognize and appreciate that they are working with a lot of interns and a lot of companies, but I wonder if putting the interns in directly contact with the supervisors sooner would have helped resolve some of the confusion.

column27: My matching process was very unpredictable, I was told that majority of community launch interns would get matched to at least one of their top five choices. It was my surprise to find out that I got matched with none of my top 10 choices. I was very upset about this because I spent a lot of time making sure that I did everything correct correctly, even when the Career eco officially launched I did not receive the link even after checking my spam or junk folder. So I reached out immediately to my Career launch hub and they sent me the link directly. However, by the time I received the link spots haven’t filled up, which is honestly not something that I could control. However, I asked if I can meet with certain internships outside of the matching fair and I was told no. Even though in one of the information sessions, they said that it was possible to meet outside of the matching fair date. In general, I’m trying to make the best out of a very unpredictable and an unfortunate situation, and I’m still grateful to at least have an internship. But I did not even rank the internship that I have on my list, and I had much bigger and higher plans for myself, and I honestly feel like I was let down.

It was the one company that I was really excited to be apart of; except now, I won't be able to, leaving me quite disppointed. Regardless, even with my current placement, I will continue to work toward meeting my supervisor’s expectations, but I believe that the system should be improved in order to more closely align with an applicant’s preferences and should not be limited to a single offer. Rather, they should be allowed to select the offer that speaks most to them.
